quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When driving in rain, what lights must you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when it rains.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase your following distance. Your vehicle will need more time to stop.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You are not required to stop.
You must slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see at least 200 feet on either side, even if you enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where you can see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see approaching traffic before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: Stop at a point where you can see approaching traffic clearly. Do not enter the intersecting roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren. If you are in an intersection, pass through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: Your car hits a parked vehicle and the owner is not there. What must you do?

options.text: You have done all that is required.
You must wait for police to arrive.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
You can leave without doing anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: Try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a curve in the road ahead.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually what color and must always be obeyed?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with black markings. Drivers must always obey these signs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is merging onto the road from the right.

questions.question: What can you do from a center turn lane?
questions.explanation: A center turn lane is only for left turns. You cannot use it to pass other vehicles or for through traffic.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect your ability to stop. Slow down when roads are slippery so you can maintain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must do. It means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the speed limit, but be careful.

questions.explanation: When it rains, snows, or sleets, roads become slippery. You should slow down even if it means driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb when parking uphill. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters. They warn you about hazards or unexpected conditions ahead.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your four-way flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map.

questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except when you have an emergency.

questions.question: When can you continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you may continue carefully through.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" happens when:

options.text: You stare at the road for a long time.
You sleep too much before driving.
You take short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stare at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis occurs when you stare straight ahead for too long without looking around. You stop paying attention to traffic and may miss cars slowing or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: At a flashing red light, you should:

options.text: Come to a full stop, then go when safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if other cars are in the intersection.
Slow down and stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which must you obey over the others?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions override all signs, signals, and road markings. This includes police officers, traffic control officers, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: You are stopped behind other vehicles at a stop sign. After the vehicles ahead pass through and there is no cross traffic, you:

options.text: May drive through without stopping again.
Must stop at the stop sign before proceeding.
May roll slowly past the stop sign.
May follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop at the stop sign before proceeding.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at the stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip this stop just because other cars have passed.

questions.question: If you get a tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Slowly stop and move to the side of the road.

questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, release the gas pedal first. Do not brake suddenly. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: The condition and type of your tires.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect how far it takes to stop.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Does not change blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not reduce blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober or lower your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: At dusk or on cloudy days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on cloudy days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of oncoming traffic and within 500 feet of vehicles ahead. Always use low beams in bad weather.
